label: main season
summary: Recommend clearance for sign-off. E1 is an undated, ground-unverified database record and is indirect evidence, but national criteria make a past-accident record inside the area a clearance target after the first visit and do not allow release by non-technical survey alone. The long-term safe-use reports and the survey team's observations are relevant absence evidence but do not remove that target.
flags: E1 has no date or other detail, and its location has not been checked on the ground; retain this uncertainty for sign-off.
The zone flag and survey priority are routing information, not evidence.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
The national criteria provide no technical survey, so clearance takes its place; evidence to target: E1.

E1.quote: The national mine action database records one or more past landmine accidents inside this area.
E1.note: The database entry is undated and its location has not been checked on the ground, so it suggests possible contamination but does not verify an accident location.

E2.quote: he has cut firewood and timber in the area every year for the past 22 years, and has never found anything or heard of an accident there.
E2.note: A first-hand land user reports repeated safe use over 22 years without a find or known accident.

E3.quote: the board has recorded no find or accident in the area in the 21 years she has held the post, and that families use land in the area every week.
E3.note: The community board president reports long-term weekly use and no recorded find or accident during her tenure.

E4.quote: The survey team walked the paths and field edges of the area and saw no items, signs, fencing or other marks of contamination.
E4.note: This is the survey team's own observation of no contamination indicators on the paths and field edges it walked.
